properties.content: Question: can hiv turn into aids Answer: Yes, HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) can turn into AIDS (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome) if left untreated. HIV is a virus that weakens the immune system by attacking and destroying CD4+ cells, which are essential for fighting infections. Over time, as the virus multiplies and the number of CD4+ cells declines, the immune system becomes severely compromised. When the CD4+ cell count falls below a certain threshold (typically 200 cells per milliliter of blood) and opportunistic infections develop, HIV is considered to have progressed to AIDS. AIDS is a life-threatening condition that makes the body vulnerable to a wide range of infections and other health problems. It's important to note that with early diagnosis and effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), HIV can be managed and progression to AIDS can be prevented. Treatment can significantly slow down the decline of CD4+ cells and improve the quality of life for people living with HIV.
